limitations: File-level edges are derived from symbol-level import relationships; alias/barrel re-exports may flatten multi-hop edges.
Internal specifiers are resolved against the importing file's directory. One that resolves to nothing is reported with resolution "unresolved" and no fileId — never guessed from a basename.

Only a small minority of 'imports' relationships carry both a source and a target symbol and brain_import.resolved_symbol_id is empty, so specifier resolution is the primary path here, not a fallback.
A file's dependent and dependency lists are capped per row; dependentsTotal and dependenciesTotal are the real sizes and the Truncated flags say the list was cut.

GO CLASSIFICATION BASIS: a Go import is internal when it equals the project's go.mod module path or starts with it; the specifier then names a PACKAGE (every .go file in one directory). The module path is read from go.mod at index time and persisted per project. When a project has no recorded module path, a domain-shaped Go specifier cannot be classified internal and is reported external with no resolution claim — the page cannot then claim Go coupling, and that absence is a classification limit, not a measurement of zero coupling.
